prompt.adult: When Jesus taught in the synagogue of His hometown, the people were offended. In 6:3, what do they call Him?
prompt.child: People in Jesus’ hometown did not believe in Him. What job did they say He had?
prompt.teen: Mark 6:3: “Is this not” whom, “the Son of Mary”?
prompt.older: According to Mark 6:3, what did the people of His hometown call Jesus?

verses.text: Is this not the carpenter, the Son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And are not His sisters here with us?” So they were offended at Him.

explanation.child: Look at the first question in verse 3.
explanation.teen: 6:3 asks a question and then names His family. Read the first question.

teaching.extended_explanation: 6:2 says many were astonished at His wisdom and mighty works. 6:3 ends, “So they were offended at Him.”
teaching.takeaway: They asked, “Is this not the carpenter, the Son of Mary?”

prompt.adult: In Mark 4:21, Jesus asks whether a lamp is brought to be put under a basket or under a bed. Where is it meant to be set?
prompt.child: Jesus said nobody hides a lamp under a basket or a bed. Where does a lamp belong?
prompt.teen: Mark 4:21: “Is it not to be set” where?
prompt.older: According to Mark 4:21, where is a lamp meant to be set?

verses.text: Also He said to them, “Is a lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be set on a lampstand?

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 21.
explanation.teen: 4:21 asks two questions. Read the end of the second.
explanation.older: It follows “Is it not to be set” in 4:21.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:22 goes on: “For there is nothing hidden which will not be revealed.”
teaching.takeaway: A lamp is “to be set on a lampstand.”

prompt.adult: Jesus rebukes those who reject God’s commandment to keep their tradition. In 7:11, what word is used for a gift that frees a man from helping his parents?
prompt.child: Jesus told some leaders they used a special word to avoid helping their parents. What was the word?
prompt.teen: Mark 7:11: “whatever profit you might have received from me is” what?
prompt.older: According to Mark 7:11, what word was spoken over what might have helped a parent?

verses.text: He said to them, “All too well you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
But you say, ‘If a man says to his father or mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban”—’ (that is, a gift to God),

explanation.child: Look near the end of verse 11.
explanation.teen: 7:11 gives the word and then its meaning. Read the word.
explanation.older: It comes just before “(that is, a gift to God)” in 7:11.

teaching.extended_explanation: 7:9 says they reject the commandment of God. 7:13 says they make the word of God of no effect through their tradition.
teaching.takeaway: They said, “Corban” (that is, a gift to God).

prompt.adult: In Mark 4:28-29 the earth yields crops by itself before the sickle is put in. Which comes first?
prompt.child: Jesus compared God’s kingdom to a field that brings up a crop by itself. What comes up first?
prompt.older: According to Mark 4:28, what does the earth yield first?

verses.text: For the earth yields crops by itself: first the blade, then the head, after that the full grain in the head.
But when the grain ripens, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 28.
explanation.teen: 4:28 lists three steps in order. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:28 then names the head and the full grain. 4:29 says the sickle goes in when the harvest has come.
teaching.takeaway: The earth yields first the blade.

prompt.adult: A father brought his son, who had a mute spirit, to Jesus. In 9:21, Jesus asked how long this had been happening. What did the father say?
prompt.child: Jesus asked a father how long his son had been sick. What did the father say?
prompt.older: According to Mark 9:21, how long had this been happening to the son?

verses.text: Then one of the crowd answered and said, “Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a mute spirit.
So He asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” And he said, “From childhood.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 21.
explanation.teen: 9:21 has Jesus’ question and then the father’s reply. Read the reply.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:17 says the boy had a mute spirit. 9:22 adds the father’s plea: “But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

prompt.adult: In 3:21 the people close to Jesus said, “He is out of His mind.” In 6:4, where does He say a prophet is not without honor except?
prompt.child: Jesus said a prophet is honored everywhere except in certain places. Name the first place He said.
prompt.teen: Mark 6:4: “A prophet is not without honor except” where?
prompt.older: Linking Mark 3:21 with 6:4, where is a prophet without honor?

verses.text: But when His own people heard about this, they went out to lay hold of Him, for they said, “He is out of His mind.”
But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his own country, among his own relatives, and in his own house.”

explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 6:4.
explanation.teen: 3:21 is the setting; 6:4 lists three places. Read the first.
explanation.older: It follows “not without honor except” in 6:4.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:21 says they went out to lay hold of Him. 6:4 goes on to name relatives and His house.
teaching.takeaway: A prophet is not without honor except in his own country.

prompt.adult: In 6:7 Jesus sent out the twelve in pairs. In 13:34, a man going to a far country gives authority to his servants and commands whom to watch?
prompt.child: Jesus told about a man who went on a trip and gave each servant work. Whom did he tell to keep watch?
prompt.older: Alongside the sending of 6:7, whom does the man of 13:34 command to watch?

verses.text: And He called the twelve to Himself, and began to send them out two by two, and gave them power over unclean spirits.
It is like a man going to a far country, who left his house and gave authority to his servants, and to each his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to watch.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 34.
explanation.teen: 6:7 is the setting; 13:34 lists what he gave his servants and then whom he commanded. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 6:7 says He gave them power over unclean spirits. 13:35 says, “Watch therefore, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming.”

prompt.adult: Scribes from Jerusalem accuse Jesus in 3:22. In 7:5, the Pharisees and scribes ask why His disciples eat bread with what?
prompt.child: Some religious leaders complained about how Jesus’ disciples ate. How did they say the disciples ate bread?
prompt.older: Set beside the accusation of 3:22, with what does 7:5 say the disciples eat bread?

verses.text: And the scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebub,” and, “By the ruler of the demons He casts out demons.”
Then the Pharisees and scribes asked Him, “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?”

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 7:5.
explanation.teen: 3:22 is the setting; 7:5 asks about the tradition and then how they eat. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “but eat bread with” in 7:5.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:22 says the scribes came down from Jerusalem. 7:5 asks why the disciples do not walk according to the tradition of the elders.
teaching.takeaway: They asked why the disciples “eat bread with unwashed hands.”
